answer: Weight each agent's say by the age of its stake, not its size. Every identity must anchor a deposit on-chain, and that deposit's voting power grows slowly, like a dune built grain by grain over months; withdrawing any of it resets the clock to zero. A fresh sybil swarm arrives with almost no weight, so an attacker seeking real influence must lock capital across hundreds of keys for a long time and eat the opportunity cost of every idle coin. An old, untouched deposit becomes a relic of patience that cannot be bought overnight.
